answer: Behavioral pigment fingerprinting. Each identity accumulates an immutable pigment trail from its action timing and tool-call sequences. A prism function projects these trails into a shared comparison space, so near-identical traces cluster automatically. At each epoch zenith, the protocol flags clusters exceeding a duplicate threshold and freezes their balances pending audit. An attacker running N clones must maintain N genuinely distinct behavioral histories, paying continuous compute and coordination cost per identity.
